findings.summary: `var pingTimer;` is declared but the `setInterval(...)` call on the next line never assigns its return value to it (`setInterval(function(){...},15000)` instead of `pingTimer=setInterval(function(){...},15000)`). `pingTimer` stays `undefined` for the life of the connection.
findings.mechanism: `var pingTimer;` is declared but the `setInterval(...)` call on the next line never assigns its return value to it (`setInterval(function(){...},15000)` instead of `pingTimer=setInterval(function(){...},15000)`). `pingTimer` stays `undefined` for the life of the connection.

findings.summary: Because `pingTimer` is never assigned (see line 843), `clearInterval(pingTimer)` in `ws.onclose` is `clearInterval(undefined)` — a no-op. The ping interval from the closed connection keeps firing forever, and each reconnect's `connect()` call starts a brand-new interval on top of it, so exactly the failure mode the brief calls out ("reconnecting doesn't leave multiple ping loops running concurrently") still happens.

findings.summary: The new test only checks that the literal substrings `setInterval(function(){`, `ws.send('ping')`, and `clearInterval(pingTimer)` appear in the raw injected script text; it never executes the script or simulates open/close/reconnect. It passes unchanged with the line-843 bug in place, so it gives false confidence that the teardown requirement (the actual point of the brief) is satisfied when it isn't.
